output.brief: Falls at the two pilot homes did rise on the dashboard, but I can't yet say the night rota caused it. Three things muddy the picture. First, both homes switched to the incident app on 1 July, the same quarter the rise appeared. The old paper system demonstrably missed some falls: a handover cross-check found three clear and three possible unreported falls in Q2. Most of the rise is in no-harm and found-on-floor falls, which fits better recording. Second, the rates are within each home's normal range, and other homes have had similar jumps that reversed. Third, the homes also changed GP practice and took frailer admissions, and none of that has been checked. Night call-bell data can't be compared with the period before June. Ashby Fold's median answer time is 3 min 40 s, but we have no baseline and no standard to judge it against. So I'm moderately unsure. I recommend not reverting the rota or halting the rollout now, and not disciplining staff or removing the app. Keep the pilot under its pause criteria. Chart falls as rates and mark the reporting change. Start manual sampling of call-bell response times. Review medication changes and admission frailty. Take the rollout decision in late January with Q4 data. Escalate sooner if harm-level falls or response times worsen.
